main_result.title: Rare mismatch certification needs an explicit top-level trial-unit contract plus an anytime-valid bound; all-pairs repeat counts can create severe pseudoreplication.

functions: Jeffreys beta-binomial mixture confidence-sequence upper endpoint for Bernoulli mismatch
fixed-sample zero-failure bound for comparison only
zero-mismatch sample planning for fixed versus continuous-peeking designs
explicit rejection of all-pairs repeat counts as Bernoulli trial counts

public_case.fingerprint: vLLM 0.26.0; torch 2.11.0+cu130; RTX 4060 Laptop sm_89; driver 595.84; Qwen3-0.6B float16; enforce-eager; VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1
observations: The reporter repeated byte-identical concurrent workloads five times against one unchanged server process and explicitly compared all ten repeat pairs, not independent first-vs-rest trials.

At 44 co-resident sequences there were three distinct logprob outputs across five repeats and five differing repeat pairs; at 45 co-resident there were two distinct outputs and three differing repeat pairs.
Emitted token ids did not diverge in the batch-invariant reproducer even though logprobs did; the report gives 188 and 128 diverging request-by-repeat-pair observations.
The same configuration could be fully reproducible in another server lifetime, so lifetime-level intermittency is part of the observed process.
A default-mode negative control failed 7/7 and included a first-token divergence at position 23, showing the client detector can observe token nondeterminism when present.
public_case.measurement_correction: The 188/128 request-by-repeat-pair counts must not be used as n in a Bernoulli confidence bound. Ten pair comparisons from five repeats reuse the same five outputs, and requests also share a concurrent workload/server lifetime. The independent or conditionally stable top-level trial/cluster must be declared before inference.

anytime_bound.reference: Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe, Sekhon, Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences; beta-binomial mixture family
anytime_bound.use: Invert M_t(p)<1/alpha for a time-uniform confidence set. This is appropriate for continuous peeking/optional stopping only under the declared Bernoulli/fingerprint trial-unit contract.

main_result.decision_rule: A repeated-inference fast path is not certified merely because pairwise mismatch count is zero. First require a predeclared top-level trial unit and fingerprint. Fail closed if the canonical protected statistic ever mismatches; if canonical repeats have zero observed mismatches, still require the anytime upper bound to lie below the canonical-instability tolerance. Then require the fast-vs-canonical mismatch upper bound below its tolerance. Never pool fingerprints without a justified common parameter contract.
main_result.why_this_matters: The mismatch hierarchy now has a measurement-validity gate. Public reproducibility reports often generate many dependent pair comparisons from only a few repeated executions; treating those pairs as independent can make rare-event certification look orders of magnitude stronger than the actual evidence.

measurement_validity_rules: Declare the statistical trial/cluster unit before reading mismatch results; all-pairs repeat comparisons are diagnostic edges, not independent Bernoulli trials.
Requests co-resident in one workload/server lifetime may share failure mechanisms and cannot automatically be counted as independent trials.
Use an anytime-valid confidence sequence when sample collection can continue until a target bound is crossed; do not repeatedly peek at a fixed-sample Clopper-Pearson-style bound.
Canonical protected-statistic instability is fail-closed; a noisy canonical target cannot certify a fast-path mismatch rate.
Keep runtime/model/hardware/batching fingerprints separate unless a common conditional mismatch parameter contract is established.
scope_guards: The beta-binomial utility is valid only under its declared Bernoulli/filtration contract; it does not repair arbitrary cluster dependence or runtime drift.
The public vLLM #51187 data do not provide enough independent top-level trials to certify a sub-percent token/sign mismatch rate, despite the much larger dependent pair-comparison counts.
No live GPU/vLLM token-divergent raw trace was obtained in this run, so the previous token->score->sign analyzer still lacks a same-fingerprint raw divergence dataset.
The default-mode first-token divergence in #51187 is a detector control, not evidence that the batch-invariant logprob-divergent trace changed tokens.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read.

frontier.action: Obtain a public raw repeated-inference artifact with actual token divergence under one fully recorded fingerprint, then run decision_stat_first_divergence_analyzer.py to measure token->score and paired-score->oriented-sign propagation.
Extend mismatch_anytime_certifier.py to accept predeclared independent cluster records and produce cluster-level bounded/e-process inference instead of requiring a scalar Bernoulli trial assumption.

Design a lifetime/fingerprint lease rule that combines canonical-stability confidence, fast-vs-canonical mismatch confidence, drift invalidation, and minimum independent-server-lifetime coverage without pooling dependent request pairs.
Extend deterministic prefix certificates to JSON/schema tool-call scorers and measure certificate-position latency versus full completion on public raw traces.

exact_next_action: Search for a raw same-fingerprint token-divergent repeated-inference trace; if none is public, advance cluster-aware rare-mismatch inference by treating workload/server-lifetime as the top-level unit rather than all-pairs repeat edges.
